scope: Qualification window only, RTX 4090 lane, across seven candidate commits of the runtime fork's port/native-lanes-on-mainline branch in one day. Each candidate installs into its own lineage state root (qwen38-4090-native) beside the shipped v0.6.0 release of that lineage; the RTX 5090 and RTX 3090 components were never started or modified, and the v0.2 incumbent lineage on the same host was found stopped and left untouched. Nothing was published: no component upload, no product release, no manifest, profile, or route change.
question: Does the graceful-stop candidate pass the RTX 4090 lane's own lifecycle qualification - including a never-published session surviving a managed restart and each rollback direction stopped the way its release declares - and does it survive an independent focused review of the new control surface?
answer: Yes, at runtime fork 63f28c95: 15/15 phases and 103/103 registered tests, after two focused review rounds (initial and remediation) whose eight confirmed findings are fixed at source and pinned by executable invariants. The lane itself found six more defects in the lifecycle handoff that no unit test or foreground probe could see, because they live in the moment a gracefully exiting wrapper hands the lifecycle back to the controller - a moment that never existed while stops were terminations.

review.class: focused (reusable internal path); reciprocal cross-family strong critic, resolver-selected
review.sequence: CR-2026-09-10-graceful-stop; initial on 708d66b9, remediation on 65c3ec0c; records, packets, scopes, receipts, and ledger under ~/reviews/omp-ninfer-graceful-stop*

initial_round.R1 P2 mitigate: the fallback decided from the runtime snapshot the stop opened with; it now reads state at each step
initial_round.R2 P1 mitigate: a shutdown that could not save a live session exited 0 and was recorded graceful; the flush now returns saved/skipped/refused and the process exits nonzero on any refusal
initial_round.R3 P2 mitigate: a terminating Stop-ScheduledTask error skipped the force-kill and the receipt; each termination step is now best-effort and the receipt is written in a finally
initial_round.U1 P1 accept: a low-privilege squatter pre-creating the Global event name: the window is milliseconds, the name is random per launch, the outcome is one refused start with a recorded reason, and reading a SYSTEM process command line from another session needs SeDebugPrivilege
initial_round.U2 P2 mitigate: concurrent Stop and Start could interleave over the GPU-owner lease; every mutating action now runs under an action lock
initial_round.U3 P1 reject: cpp-httplib 0.18.3 ThreadPool::shutdown joins every worker before listen returns; the dependency was outside the bound paths

remediation_round.R1 P1 mitigate: Request-ManagedStop caught only the not-found case; it now returns signalled/absent/failed and never throws, and delivery runs inside the fail-closed scope
remediation_round.R2 P1 mitigate: a previous launch's shutdown report could be read as this launch's; the wrapper mints a launch identity carried in the event name and runtime.json, the server echoes it, and the controller accepts only a matching report
remediation_round.R3 P1 mitigate: the scheduled task retries a failed wrapper, so a nonzero exit after a requested stop would have been relaunched; a wrapper that finds this launch's report exits clean and leaves the verdict to the stop receipt
remediation_round.R4 P1 mitigate: the uninstall released the action lock between its stop and the task removal; both now run under one scoped lock and the uninstall asserts no owned process survives
remediation_round.R5 P1 mitigate: Copy-InstalledRelease rebuilt every existing record from a field list that predates the channel, so installing the next release stripped managed_stop from every 0.6.1 incumbent - proven on the host: every record installed before 63f28c95 had already lost it, and 65c3ec0c kept it through the 63f28c95 installer
remediation_round.U1 P1 resolved by observation: the release logs directory carries exactly two inherited ACEs, SYSTEM and Administrators, FullControl; no standard-user ACE exists, so a low-privilege principal cannot create, replace, or lock the report
remediation_round.U2 P2 accept: whether draining plus saving every live session always fits the 900 s bound at the configured 1,024-record store: the bound is the qualification's own restart timeout, the outcome at the bound is the pre-existing termination, and the receipt records it; no saturated-store measurement was taken

review.disposition: no in-scope residual P0/P1; the credential path is unchanged (the stop event admits only SYSTEM and Administrators, the report directory the same); sequence closed
